access_note: EU Login with two-factor authentication (mobile phone number or EU Login app) is required since the Commission protected access; some data restricted to authorised users.
description: eMARS is the European Commission's database of major industrial accidents involving dangerous substances, run by the Joint Research Centre's Major Accident Hazards Bureau. Its purpose is to collect the reports that countries submit on major accidents at establishments covered by the Seveso Directive, so that authorities and industry can learn from them; the report fields could not be read without a login. Coverage is European, per event. On 26 September 2026 the site stated that access to eMARS and eSPIRS is protected by EU Login with two-factor authentication using a mobile phone number or app; after login users find the tools according to their authorisation level. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): CC-BY-4.0 (European Commission reuse policy: EU-owned content under CC BY 4.0 unless otherwise noted). Access is free of charge. Caveats: reporting depends on national authorities, some fields are confidential and visible only to authorised users, and the login requirement limits scripted access. For simulation it is an event record of industrial and natech accidents for estimating failure frequencies, consequences and cascading effects on neighbouring infrastructure. Related catalogue records include eSPIRS, the ARIA database of France and the JRC eNATECH database.
